decisions.name: whether a new passport keeps the battery's unique identifier
decisions.question: When a battery that is placed on the market again receives a new battery passport (Art. 77(7)), does it keep its unique identifier, with the new passport told apart by a battery passport identifier (DIN 6.1.2.2 a) and 6.1.2.1 a)), or does the new passport receive a new unique identifier that differs from the identifier of every original passport (vision invariant 5, StR-LIFE-027, "New unique identifier for the new passport")?
decisions.why: DIN 6.1.2.2 a) requires the QR code to link to 'a persistent unique battery identifier', and DIN 6.1.2.1 a) adds a separate battery passport identifier 'as there might be multiple battery passports attributed to one physical battery', which reads as one battery identifier across successive passports. The vision (invariant 5 and section 5) gives the new passport 'a new unique identifier', and StR-LIFE-027 ("New unique identifier for the new passport") requires it to differ from every original passport's. StR-PASS-019 ("Unique identifier persistent for the life of the passport") limits the persistence to changes that create no new passport, which matches the vision but not the unqualified DIN text. The Regulation does not decide: Art. 77(3) says only that the economic operator placing the battery on the market attributes the unique identifier, and Art. 13(9) requires new labels for a treated battery. Not settled for the stored text, because DIN never states the case of a new passport (the persistence across passports is a reading of 6.1.2.1 a)) and Q-02 (whether the DIN additions bind the dataset) is open. If the persistent reading is chosen, the vision's invariant 5 changes first, then StR-LIFE-027 and StR-PASS-019.

answer.text: Derived from Francesco's expressed intent ("the open decisions must be derived by the intent expressed by me" (Francesco, 2026-10-26)): A battery that receives a new battery passport because it is placed on the market again after preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing receives a new unique identifier, which differs from the identifier of every original passport, and the new passport is linked to the original passport or passports. Only a repair of a battery that is not waste keeps the passport and its unique identifier.

decisions.question: Q-LIFE-09 extended to the passport content: on the new passport of a treated battery, are the manufacturer identifier and information, the battery category and the EU declaration of conformity held for a new battery model of the treating operator, or for the individual battery? decisions.why: StR-LIFE-029 ("New passport takes over the battery model") gives the new passport the battery model of the original battery. StR-PASS-037 ("Manufacturer identifier relating to the battery model"), StR-PASS-061 ("Battery category of the battery model") and StR-PASS-086 ("EU declaration of conformity of the battery model") relate the manufacturer identifier, the category and the declaration of conformity to the battery model, as DIN states. decisions.name: how the dataset delivers each field's access group
decisions.question: In which form shall the application deliver the access group of each field of the battery passport dataset, given that no field of the seven IDTA-02035 aspect models carries one: an additional aspect model of the application on the battery's twins (CX-0160 base 1.2) that names the access group for each twin level, field path and list element; one submodel per access group, each offered with its own access policy; or no marking, the passport service provider applying the access groups itself?
decisions.why: CX-0160 1.1.0 puts 'full regulatory-compliance e.g. for providing public information without access-restrictions' out of scope (base 1.1, CX-0160-3 1.1) and gives the intermediary that publishes the passport 'role-based access control on restricted data' (CX-0160-3 5.2); its base 1.2 (non-normative) lets data owners 'add complementary information via additional aspect models'. The access groups mix inside one aspect (the Digital Nameplate holds public identification beside the legitimate-interest LifeCycleStage and DateOfPuttingIntoService), inside one list element (a Material Composition BatteryMaterials entry carries the public critical raw material beside the restricted mass and location), inside one field (Circularity SafetyMeasures.SafetyInstructions references both the public safety instructions for waste batteries of Art. 74(1)(d), SyR-PASS-137, "Safety instructions to handle waste batteries, public", and the restricted safety measures of Annex XIII point 2(d), SyR-PASS-115, "Safety measures for the battery model, restricted") and across twin levels (a Technical Data value is public as a model value under Annex XIII point 1 and legitimate interest as the individual battery's value under point 4(a), SyR-PASS-149, "Individual battery performance values marked legitimate interest"). A connector access policy works per data offer, and the finest data asset of CX-0160 base 4.1 is one submodel, so one offer per access group separates the groups only by splitting the payloads of the seven models. Today only the passport demo holds tiers (EL-PASSPORTDEMO, the column access matrix of the battery passport application), and decisions.json holds no question on the form. The passport demo screens take each field's tier from the same marking (SyR-PASS-207, "Passport screens show each field only to its access group"); the owner-rules and operations requirements on tier-driven visibility (SyR-DEV-074, "Passport field visibility decided by its access tier", SyR-QUAL-009, "Passport demo components render for every role without error") must use the same source. Every passport-content measure that checks 'the access marking gives' a group is recorded as not run until this is answered.

SyR-DEV-042 ("Every API response in the success or error envelope") keeps the rule unweakened, and VM-SYS-DEV-016 ("Response envelope and status codes of every route") reports those success bodies apart until Francesco rules. Either way the failure bodies of the two submodel routes answer error as a string in the battery passport application on 2026-10-22 and fail the rule (known deviation of SyR-DEV-042).
options: Yes: a route that serves an aspect payload answers it bare on success, and the project guidelines of the battery passport application's API design names the exception.
No: every response keeps the envelope, and the connector-facing aspect routes are changed, with the consequences for CX-0136 and the SAMM conformance stated first.

The CX-Titan texts bind the data layer: CX-0136 requires the value-only PCF JSON as the synchronous response body, and CX-0002 the value-only serialization of a submodel.

decisions.name: who reads the state of health and battery status under the draft Article 77(9) act
decisions.question: Article 1(4) of the draft Implementing Regulation on access to battery passport information (SRC-EU-DRAFT-IMPL-77-9, Ares(2026)9814179, feedback until 16 November 2026) names only the purchaser of the battery and a third party acting on the purchaser's behalf as persons with a legitimate interest in the Annex XIII point 4 information (state of health and battery status). Article 1(1) and 1(2) of the draft give repairers, remanufacturers, repurposers, waste treatment operators and recyclers the point 2 information of the battery model only. ADR 0002 and the project guidelines of the battery passport application open the point 4 data to every used-battery operator (second_use, repurposer, remanufacturer, recycler) and to the manufacturer. Does the application follow the draft, keep ADR 0002, or follow the draft and send feedback to the Commission before 16 November 2026?
decisions.why: ADR 0002 (dynamic durability data in the legitimate-interest tier) and the column access matrix grant the Annex XIII point 4 columns to the used-battery operators, while the draft Article 77(9) act grants them only to the purchaser and the purchaser's agent. Draft Article 2(4)(c) lets the purchaser share point 4 information with prospective purchasers, which matches the owner's sharing act of the marketplace demo (batteries.for_sale). Decision Q-018 (authority access to state of health and battery status) waits for this act; the draft names no authority as a person with a legitimate interest, and draft Article 2(4)(c) lets the purchaser share point 4 information with the market surveillance authorities.
options: A: follow the draft once the Commission adopts the act: the Annex XIII point 4 data are readable by the purchaser (the owner) and the owner's agent only, a used-battery operator reads them only through the owner's sharing act (draft Art. 2(4)(c)), and a new ADR supersedes ADR 0002.
B: keep ADR 0002 until the act is adopted, and change nothing now.

C: option A for the target design, and Francesco sends feedback on the Have Your Say page before 16 November 2026 asking the Commission to name the operators of Art. 77(2), third subparagraph, point (a), for the point 4 data that preparation for re-use, repurposing and remanufacturing need.
decisions.recommendation: Option C: the draft is the only text that names the persons of Art. 77(2)(c), so the target design follows the draft. The marketplace sharing act already fits draft Art. 2(4)(c), and the feedback window is the moment to raise the gap for second-life operators.

answer.text: "Option A: the company which prepares the battery will also be the one which in interested in buying the battery. The previous owner who wants to sell the battery is the data owner, so according to GDPR he must consent to the data usage, so I understand the intent of the legislator" (Francesco, 2026-11-05, requirements/Owner_instructions-Francesco_verbatim/2026-11-05_after_first_passport_downloads_paid_standards_and_q1002.md). The target design follows draft Article 1(4) of the Article 77(9) implementing act (SRC-EU-DRAFT-IMPL-77-9) once the Commission adopts the act: the Annex XIII point 4 data of an individual battery (performance and durability values, state of health, battery status, usage data) are readable by the purchaser of the battery and by a third party acting on the purchaser's behalf; a repairer, remanufacturer, repurposer, waste treatment operator, recycler or manufacturer reads them only when the owner shares them as a prospective purchaser (draft Article 2(4)(c)), which the marketplace flag batteries.for_sale already models. No feedback is sent to the Commission. ADR 0002 stays in force until the act is adopted; a new ADR then supersedes it, and step 3 of the after-first-passport work derives the requirements of the target design.

decisions.name: how the producers of a battery learn its recycling result after re-use or remanufacturing
decisions.question: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/606 (SRC-EU-2025-606) sets the methodology and the documentation format of the recycling efficiency and the recovery of materials from waste batteries. Francesco's premise of 2026-11-05: the manufacturers and economic operators must report statistics on the recycling of their batteries, so they must receive notifications and data when their batteries are recycled, even after the batteries have been re-used or remanufactured. Which party receives the recycling result of a battery whose passport has predecessors, and through which channel?
decisions.why: The open point of Francesco's task for the Digital Product Passport Expert Group: CX-0160 1.1.0 defines no notification of the end of a passport, and the application's notifyRemoteManufacturers broadcasts a custom payload to every company. The citation catalogue checks the premise against Art. 56, 61, 75 and 76 and Recital (102) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 before a recommendation.
options: A: relay along the lineage chain, each operator forwarding a CX-0151 notification to the operator of the predecessor passport.
B: direct notice from the recycler, which walks the predecessor links and notifies each operator found through the BPN Discovery Service and the Connector Discovery Service.
C: subscription carried forward: an operator subscribes to end-of-life events on its twin, and each new passport inherits the subscriptions.
D: publish and pull: the final passport and its twin publish the end of the passport and the recovered materials, and producers query the twins of their own passports.
decisions.recommendation: Decided after the citation catalogue (step 2) checks the premise and the system requirements (step 3) are derived.

answer.text: "Approve all" (Francesco, 2026-11-09, requirements/Owner_instructions-Francesco_verbatim/2026-11-09_forward_link_and_use_case_5.md), accepting option B plus D. The first recycler, or the treatment operator acting for the producer, sends a CX-0151 notification with the end of the passport and the recovered materials recorded for the battery to the producer of the passport that the recycling ends; that producer finances the reporting (Art. 56(4)(d)) and its producer responsibility organisation publishes the recycling efficiencies of its producers (Art. 57(5)). The recycler may also notify the economic operator responsible for each predecessor passport that the backward links reach, when a contract with that operator exists, which serves the cost sharing of Art. 56(5) and use case UC-5a. The end of the passport is published on the final passport dataset and its digital twin (SyR-LIFE-011, SyR-LIFE-127). No stored text obliges the recycler to report to a manufacturer, so the notices rest on the producer's financing and on contracts.

decisions.name: which producer takes over the passport of a second-life battery that becomes waste
decisions.question: Art. 77(7), second subparagraph, of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 transfers the responsibility for the passport of a battery that becomes waste "either to the producer", to the producer responsibility organisation, or to the waste management operator. A battery placed on the market again after preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing has two producers: the original producer and the second-life operator, which Art. 56(2) makes "the producer of such battery". Which producer receives the passport responsibility when such a battery becomes waste?
decisions.why: The step 2 citation catalogue (the citation catalogue, section 4) found that Art. 77(7) does not name which producer, and that recital 2 of the draft Art. 77(9) act repeats the wording. The answer decides whom the waste status transfer of the lifecycle engine addresses and whom the recycler reaches for decision Q-1006 (how the producers of a battery learn its recycling result).
options: A: the producer of the passport that is current when the battery becomes waste, which is the second-life operator for a battery placed on the market again (Art. 56(2), Art. 38(11)), and the original producer for a battery that is only re-used (Recital 16).
B: the original producer of the first passport in every case.
decisions.recommendation: Option A: Art. 56(2) makes the second-life operator the producer with the extended producer responsibility for the battery it places on the market, and Recital 102 states that the original producer should not bear the costs of the battery's later life.

answer.text: "Accept all four" (Francesco, 2026-11-05, requirements/Owner_instructions-Francesco_verbatim/2026-11-05_after_first_passport_downloads_paid_standards_and_q1002.md), accepting the recommendation. Option A. When a battery becomes waste, the passport responsibility of Art. 77(7), second subparagraph, goes to the producer of the passport that is current at that moment (or its producer responsibility organisation or selected waste management operator): the second-life operator for a battery placed on the market again after preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing (Art. 56(2), Art. 38(11)), and the original producer for a battery that is only re-used (Recital 16).

decisions.name: whether the original passport records a link to its successor passport
decisions.question: Art. 77(7) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 requires the new passport to be "linked to the battery passport or passports of the original battery or batteries", which is a link from the new passport back to the original passports. Should the original passport also record a link forward to its successor, and who writes that link, given that Art. 78(c) gives the storage of the original passport to its own economic operator and Art. 78(f) restricts the right to modify a passport?
decisions.why: The step 2 citation catalogue (the citation catalogue, section 4) found no text that states the direction, the content or the writer of the link. A forward link lets a reader of an original passport find the later life of the battery; writing the forward link needs the original economic operator, because the second-life operator has no right to modify the original passport.
options: A: the backward link only, on the new passport, as Art. 77(7) states; the data layer answers the forward question from its lineage records.
B: the backward link, and the original economic operator adds a forward link to the original passport when the second-life operator notifies it.
decisions.recommendation: Option A: Art. 77(7) requires the backward link only, and option B would make the second-life operator depend on the original operator's action. Step 3 checks option A against the alternatives of decision Q-1006, because a recycler notice along the predecessor links needs only the backward links.

answer.text: "agreed to all your 3 points: 1. Decision Q-1008 revised: the original issuer may write a forward link into its own passport, after the second-life operator's notice. 2. decisions.name: whether the battery identifier changes when a new passport is issued
decisions.question: Art. 77(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 assigns the unique identifier to the battery passport, and decision Q-969 gives every new passport a new unique identifier. DIN DKE SPEC 99100 §6.1.2.2 a) calls the battery identifier (the serial number) persistent. Does the battery identifier change when a new passport is issued after preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing?
decisions.why: The independent review of draft 0.1 of the CX-0160 amendment proposal (question 6) found that the proposal did not say which identifier changes, and that DIN DKE SPEC 99100 §6.1.2.2 a) calls the battery identifier persistent.
options: A: the passport identifier is new for every new passport; the battery identifier persists after preparation for re-use and after repurposing of one battery; a battery remanufactured or assembled from several batteries gets a new battery identifier.
